threats.attackScenario: The tutorial-browse flow serves /tutorial/<page> with no authentication check in app/routes/tutorial.js:31-36, and app/views/tutorial/a7.html:31 prints the admin username and password in plain text, so an unauthenticated attacker fetches GET /tutorial/a7, reads `user: admin, password: Admin_123`, and logs in to /benefits as the administrator.
assumptions: The deployed instance still has the documented default admin account with the unchanged password.
threats.impactReason: The disclosed credentials grant administrative access to the benefits module and every employee's records.

threats.title: Tutorial page rendering accepts a template name derived from the route path without output security headers
threats.asset: tutorial content pages rendered in the user's browser
threats.attackScenario: GET /tutorial/<page> at app/routes/tutorial.js:31 renders `tutorial/${page}` templates that embed third-party YouTube iframes (app/views/tutorial/ssrf.html:23) and are returned without Content-Security-Policy or X-Frame-Options, so an attacker frames /tutorial/a7 inside a lookalike page and overlays it to mislead a logged-in employee, or loads hostile framed content alongside the tutorial markup.
assumptions: No reverse proxy or upstream middleware adds Content-Security-Policy or X-Frame-Options headers to responses from this router.
threats.impactReason: Only static tutorial content is affected; the main risk is clickjacking or framing of the app chrome rather than direct data loss.
threats.likelihoodReason: Reachable without authentication, but exploitation requires luring a user and offers limited gain on static pages.

mitigation.summary: Send framing and content-security headers for tutorial responses.
steps: Add helmet (or explicit res.set calls) in app/routes/tutorial.js to emit Content-Security-Policy with frame-ancestors 'self' and X-Frame-Options: DENY.
Restrict the allowed page list lookup to the existing `pages` array so no path value can select an unexpected template.

threats.title: Unauthenticated /tutorial pages disclose the application's default admin credentials
threats.asset: default admin account credentials (user: admin, password: Admin_123)
threats.attackScenario: The tutorial router registers GET /tutorial/a7 at app/routes/tutorial.js:31 with no isLoggedIn middleware, so an anonymous attacker requests /tutorial/a7, reads the literal admin credentials printed at app/views/tutorial/a7.html:31, and then signs in to the application's admin account and reaches the /benefits module.
assumptions: The deployed instance still has the default admin account with the password shown in the tutorial page.
threats.impactReason: The disclosed credentials grant administrative access to employee benefits and user data if the default account was never rotated.
threats.likelihoodReason: The page is served without authentication and the credentials appear in plain text in the rendered HTML.

mitigation.summary: Remove live credentials from the tutorial content and gate the tutorial router.
steps: Replace the literal 'user: admin, password: Admin_123' text at app/views/tutorial/a7.html:31 with a placeholder.
Mount the router from app/routes/tutorial.js behind the existing isLoggedIn middleware, or disable it entirely outside development via the environment check in config/config.js.
Rotate the seeded admin password so the documented default no longer works.

threats.title: Login credentials submitted over plaintext HTTP can be captured or altered in transit
threats.asset: login credentials and the resulting session cookie
threats.attackScenario: The POST /login flow to the handler at app/routes/index.js:34 carries userName and password over HTTP across a trust boundary, so an attacker on the same café Wi-Fi or upstream network sniffs the request body, harvests the credentials and the Set-Cookie session identifier returned by the handler, and replays the cookie to impersonate the victim, including an account whose isAdmin flag is set.
assumptions: No TLS termination is in place, so traffic including credentials and sensitive personal data is sent over plain HTTP.
The application is served over plain HTTP with no TLS terminating proxy or HSTS in front of it.
threats.impactReason: Captured credentials and session identifiers give full account takeover, including admin-flagged accounts.
threats.likelihoodReason: Requires a network position on the victim's path, but the credentials are sent in the clear on every login with no protection. Answer applied: no answer: the developer skipped or was unsure, so the cautious default applies.

mitigation.summary: Force TLS for the login flow and mark the session cookie secure.
steps: Terminate HTTPS for the app and redirect all HTTP requests to HTTPS before they reach the /login route registered in app/routes/index.js.
Set `cookie: { secure: true, httpOnly: true, sameSite: 'lax' }` on the express-session configuration used by app/routes/session.js.
Add a Strict-Transport-Security response header so browsers never resend credentials over HTTP.

threats.title: Unthrottled POST /login flow allows credential stuffing and password brute force
threats.asset: user accounts and their session identifiers
threats.attackScenario: An attacker scripts thousands of POST /login requests to the handler at app/routes/index.js:34 with a leaked username/password list; because each request runs validateLogin (app/data/user-dao.js:57) against the users collection with no attempt counter, lockout or delay, the attacker both guesses valid credentials and saturates the single Node process and Mongo connection so legitimate logins stall.
assumptions: No rate limiting, CAPTCHA or account lockout is applied in front of the /login route.
threats.impactReason: Successful guessing yields full account takeover, and sustained request volume degrades login availability for all users.
threats.likelihoodReason: The endpoint is unauthenticated, publicly reachable and trivially scriptable.

mitigation.summary: Add per-IP and per-account throttling plus lockout to the login handler.
steps: Apply an express rate-limit middleware to the POST /login route in app/routes/index.js:34.
Track consecutive failed attempts per userName in the users collection and refuse authentication in handleLoginRequest (app/routes/session.js:53) after a threshold, with exponential backoff.
Log throttled attempts so repeated bursts can be alerted on.

threats.title: Unthrottled POST /signup flow permits mass account creation and storage exhaustion
threats.asset: the users collection and application availability
threats.attackScenario: An attacker loops POST /signup requests at app/routes/index.js:38; each one calls UserDAO.addUser, which performs a getNextSequence write and a users insert (app/data/user-dao.js:38-46) with no CAPTCHA or per-IP limit, letting the attacker create unlimited accounts that squat usernames and grow the users collection until the database fills.
assumptions: No CAPTCHA, email verification or rate limiting guards the /signup route.
threats.impactReason: Database bloat and username squatting degrade service and pollute the account namespace, though no existing data is disclosed.
threats.likelihoodReason: Signup is unauthenticated and a trivial script can issue requests continuously.

mitigation.summary: Throttle and verify account creation on the signup route.
steps: Apply an express rate-limit middleware to POST /signup in app/routes/index.js:38, keyed by client IP.
Require email verification before the account created in app/data/user-dao.js:addUser becomes usable for login.
Add a CAPTCHA or proof-of-work challenge to the form rendered by app/views/signup.html.

threats.title: Signup credentials stored in plaintext after crossing the POST /signup flow
threats.asset: user account passwords
threats.attackScenario: The chosen password carried by POST /signup is written straight into the users collection at app/data/user-dao.js:25, where the bcrypt hashing call is left commented out at lines 27-30, so an attacker who obtains any read access to the Mongo users collection (backup copy, injection, or an exposed instance) reads every account's cleartext password and replays it against /login and other sites.
assumptions: The POST /signup handler passes the submitted password through to UserDAO.addUser without hashing it first.
threats.impactReason: Every user's cleartext password, including admin accounts, is exposed and reusable elsewhere.
threats.likelihoodReason: Signup is publicly reachable and the storage path unconditionally persists the raw password field.

mitigation.summary: Hash signup passwords with the bcrypt library already in the project before persisting them.
steps: Uncomment and use `password: bcrypt.hashSync(password, bcrypt.genSaltSync())` in the user document built at app/data/user-dao.js:20-31 and delete the raw `password` field.
Change validateLogin in app/data/user-dao.js:57 to use bcrypt.compareSync against the stored hash.
Migrate existing stored cleartext passwords by rehashing them on next successful login and forcing a reset.
